engineering_content.technology_domain: Catheter Mechanics + Hydraulic Actuation + Tissue Interaction

system_architecture.description: Steerable CSF shunt catheter with hydraulic actuation for autonomous navigation during placement. R1 fix: original P-22 assumed fully autonomous navigation without addressing buckling failure modes; R1 redesign adds buckling analysis, tissue damage safety, and human-in-the-loop fallback.

subsystems.function: Carries CSF flow + houses steering lumens + sensor channels

subsystems.name: Hydraulic steering actuator
subsystems.function: Inflatable/deflatable balloon or bellows at catheter tip; bends catheter when pressurized
subsystems.evidence_source: External precedent (Advanced Science 2025 hydraulically steerable catheter)

subsystems.name: Tip position sensor
subsystems.function: Measures catheter tip position and orientation for closed-loop navigation

subsystems.name: Navigation controller
subsystems.function: Closed-loop controller computing actuator pressures to track target trajectory; human-in-the-loop fallback (R1 fix)

key_equations: P_cr = (pi^2 * E * I) / L^2           [elastic column buckling]
Bending radius: R_bend = EI / M   [moment-curvature relationship]
mechanical_model.buckling_regime: Catheter subject to axial compression during insertion; Euler buckling load P_cr = pi^2 * E * I / L^2 sets maximum axial force before buckling
mechanical_model.tissue_interaction: Catheter-tissue contact forces must remain below tissue damage threshold (UNKNOWN specific threshold)
mechanical_model.critical_parameter: EI (flexural rigidity), actuator force, buckling threshold
mechanical_model.R1_correction: Original P-22 assumed unlimited autonomous navigation; R1 redesign adds buckling failure mode + tissue safety + human-in-the-loop fallback

mechanism_architecture.physical_changes: Hydraulic pressure in steering lumen deflects catheter tip; coordinated multi-lumen pressure changes navigate catheter through anatomy
mechanism_architecture.key_physics: Catheter bending governed by beam theory: curvature kappa = M / (E*I), where M is bending moment from actuator force. Buckling failure when axial compression exceeds Euler load P_cr = pi^2*E*I/L^2.

navigation_model.input: Target trajectory (from preoperative imaging) + sensed tip position
navigation_model.model: Closed-loop control: delta = target - sensed; controller computes actuator pressures; catheter bends to reduce delta
navigation_model.safety_envelope: Max axial force < P_cr (buckling); max contact force < tissue damage threshold (UNKNOWN); human-in-the-loop fallback if trajectory diverges

governing_model.summary: Hydraulic beam steering with buckling constraint. Catheter is modeled as flexible beam with hydraulically-actuated bending moment; axial compression limited by Euler buckling.
equations: P_cr = (pi^2 * E * I) / L^2           [elastic column buckling]
M_tip = F_hydraulic * d_moment_arm   [bending moment at tip]
assumptions: Tissue is elastic with damage threshold (UNKNOWN specific value)
boundary_conditions: Proximal: insertion force applied by clinician/robot
Distal: free tip with actuator moment
parameter_sensitivities: EI (flexural rigidity) — too stiff: cannot bend; too soft: buckles easily
L (length) — P_cr scales as 1/L^2; longer catheter buckles more easily
Actuator area A — linear scaling of force
Tissue stiffness — affects contact force magnitude
failure_regimes: Tissue damage (contact force > threshold) — puncture or trauma
Actuator saturation — cannot achieve required bending
Navigation error — trajectory diverges from target

engineering_core.external_precedent: EXTERNAL_PRECEDENT ≠ INVENTION_VALIDATION — published steerable catheter literature (Advanced Science 2025, PMC9809155) establishes that hydraulic steerable catheters are technically feasible. It does NOT establish that the proposed autonomous navigation system achieves clinically useful accuracy or safety in CSF shunt placement.
